summary: I checked 9 of the strongest leads with searches. Nothing qualifies for a Lane C long-form today, because no fresh randomized result came out in the last 48 h. Retatrutide vs semaglutide (TRANSCEND-T2D-2) was announced on Oct 28. HCPLive confirms the topline numbers, and it isn't peer-reviewed yet. It's peaking in mainstream news, so it fits a 13:00 retatrutide Short. The biggest early bet is ObesityWeek 2026 in November. Novo says it will present new CagriSema data there, and full REDEFINE 4 results (CagriSema vs tirzepatide in obesity) are expected at the meeting. If they appear, that becomes a Lane C long-form. The topic should first be checked against Novo's ObesityWeek release. Lane A should follow the playbook queue: stopping tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-4), then hair loss, then protein. Two seasonal hooks are building: Thanksgiving eating (peaks around Nov 20–27) and cold and flu season while on tirzepatide (Yahoo Health, Oct 31). New body-worry Short ideas: telling your dentist before sedation (Yahoo, Oct 31), older adults and frailty (JAMA, Oct 30), and mood. The tirzepatide heart approval in the GreaterGood item is old news (FDA approved it on Aug 28), so I skipped it. Rejected: online and $99 GLP-1 programs, compounded pricing, 'research buyer' retatrutide, and cost or coverage stories (banned lane).

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain week 36 to 88 on placebo), refreshed by the Metabolites regain review (Oct 9) and a new semaglutide persistence cohort (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 29)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, already next in the queue. Open with 'You're doing well on tirzepatide and wonder what happens if you stop' and give the answer in 15 s: in SURMOUNT-4, people switched to placebo regained some weight, and those who stayed on lost more. Frame it calmly: obesity is a chronic condition, and 'stay on it' is not the only lever (protein, strength, habits). Say 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own' plus the prescriber line.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg in type 2 diabetes (TRANSCEND-T2D-2, 1,298 adults, 80 weeks, topline Oct 28): HbA1c −2.2 vs −1.8 points; weight −19.5% (9 mg) and −20.9% (12 mg) vs −9.4%; stopped for side effects 4.8% and 7.9% vs 2.7%
candidates.angle: A 13:00 'what's confirmed?' retatrutide Short with a loop ending. Give the benefit and the trade-off together: more weight loss, but more people stopped because of side effects, and dysesthesia (unusual skin sensations) in 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%. Say it's a type 2 diabetes population, topline only, not yet peer-reviewed, and not approved. No long-form: it's past the 48 h window and it's not a tirzepatide arm.
candidates.why_now: Reuters, USA Today, NY Post, ABC7 and Medscape all covered it (Oct 28–31), and News18 is still writing about it today. The side-effect and discontinuation angle (Medical Daily) is less covered than the 'doubles Ozempic' headline.

candidates.topic: Catching a cold or stomach bug on tirzepatide: why you may get dehydrated faster and why to check cold medicines with a pharmacist (Yahoo Health, Oct 31)
candidates.angle: A seasonal 08:00 body-worry Short, possibly a Lane A long-form later. Explain that reduced thirst and appetite plus vomiting or diarrhea can add up to dehydration, which the label warns can affect the kidneys. Some cold remedies (decongestants, sugary syrups) deserve a quick pharmacist check. Never tell people to skip or hold doses; say 'ask your prescriber what to do if you're sick'.
